prompt: Which three primitives does Marginalia's server offer?

choices.text: Tools, resources and a prompt
choices.why: Right. get_order and search_help, help://{article_id}, and reply_to_customer.

choices.text: Tools, sampling and roots, as the 2026-07-28 revision recommends for new servers
choices.why: Sampling and roots are client features, and both are deprecated.

choices.text: Three tools, each a decorated function
choices.why: It has two tools; the other primitives are different kinds of thing.

choices.text: A model, a loop and tools
choices.why: Those belong to a host; the server has no model.

prompt: How does try_server.py reach the server without starting a subprocess?

choices.text: It imports shop.py and calls get_order directly
choices.why: It goes through a real MCP client and the server's handlers.

choices.text: Client(server) connects in-process
choices.why: Right. Given the server object, the client reaches the same handlers a host's requests do.

choices.text: Through HTTP on port 8700, which the server opens automatically when it is imported
choices.why: Nothing listens on a port here.

choices.text: Through Ollama on port 11434
choices.why: No model takes part in this lesson.

prompt: Why does OrderId put the pattern in the type annotation?

choices.text: Because pydantic refuses strings without a pattern
choices.why: A plain str is accepted; the pattern is a choice.

choices.text: To make the tool list shorter
choices.why: It makes the schema longer, on purpose.

choices.text: So that shop.py does not need to check the id
choices.why: shop.py still raises for an order that does not exist.

choices.text: One annotation becomes both the schema and the check
choices.why: Right. The model is told the rule, and the two cannot drift apart.

prompt: What may a host do with readOnlyHint from a server it does not trust?

choices.text: Skip confirmation for the tool, since the server says it changes nothing
choices.why: The specification says hints from untrusted servers are untrusted.

choices.text: Nothing; hints are removed by the protocol
choices.why: They are in the tool list.

choices.text: Treat it as the server's description of itself, not as a guarantee
choices.why: Right. The decision about a person stays with the host.

choices.text: Forward it to the model as an instruction
choices.why: A hint is metadata for the host, not an instruction.

prompt: Why did customer_id not reach the client, although the database row has it?

choices.text: Order declares the fields that leave the server, and it is not one
choices.why: Right. The output type is an allow list.

choices.text: Because the SDK removes personal data automatically
choices.why: The SDK knows nothing about personal data.

choices.text: Because the client asked for fewer fields in its tools/call request
choices.why: The request carried only order_id.

choices.text: Because shop.get_order hides it
choices.why: shop.get_order returns it; the server dropped it.

prompt: A tool result's JSON object matching the output schema is in the field `___`.
Why did the M-9999 call explain itself here, when lesson 13's server said only 'Error executing tool get_order'?

choices.text: Because this server uses a newer SDK version than lesson 13's did
choices.why: Both use mcp 2.3.0.

choices.text: Because the client asked for details
choices.why: The request is the same.

choices.text: Because the database returned a friendlier error
choices.why: shop.py raised the same LookupError.

choices.text: It raised ToolError, whose text is passed on
choices.why: Right. ToolError is the one exception whose text reaches the client; any other is a crash, with details kept on the server.

prompt: What happened to the call with order_id '1043'?

choices.text: It was refused by validation before the function ran
choices.why: Right. The message named the pattern; the database was not touched.

choices.text: It returned order M-1043
choices.why: Nothing adds the prefix.

choices.text: It crashed the server
choices.why: The server answered the next request.

choices.text: It returned an empty Order, with every field set to null
choices.why: No Order was built.

prompt: What is the difference between a tool and a resource?

choices.text: A tool returns text and a resource returns JSON
choices.why: Either can return either.

choices.text: Resources are faster
choices.why: Speed is not the distinction.

choices.text: A model asks for a tool; a host reads a resource
choices.why: Right. Who decides is what differs.

choices.text: Resources only work over HTTP, because they are addressed by URIs
choices.why: help://h14 was read in-process.

prompt: Why is help_article safe against a URI such as help://../data/shop.db?

choices.text: Because help:// URIs cannot contain dots
choices.why: Dots are allowed; the handler never uses them as a path.

choices.text: It looks ids up in a dictionary and never builds a path
choices.why: Right. And the SDK's ResourceSecurity refuses traversal in template parameters by default.

choices.text: Because the server runs as root
choices.why: It runs as ana, which is why a path check would matter.

choices.text: Because the client checks URIs before sending them
choices.why: The server cannot rely on that.

prompt: How many help articles does the resource template stand for?
Who chooses a prompt, in MCP's division of the primitives?

choices.text: The model, when it needs instructions
choices.why: The model asks for tools; a person picks prompts.

choices.text: The server, at start-up, sending each prompt as the client connects
choices.why: The server only offers prompts; it does not push them.

choices.text: Ollama
choices.why: No model is involved in choosing.

choices.text: A person
choices.why: Right. A host shows prompts as something like slash commands.

prompt: The prompt says 'look the order up with get_order'. Does that let the model call get_order?

choices.text: Yes; a prompt from a server grants its tools
choices.why: Prompts grant nothing.

choices.text: No: that is the host's call
choices.why: Right. A prompt is text, not a permission.

choices.text: Only if the person typed the order id
choices.why: The argument fills the text; it decides nothing about calls.

choices.text: Yes, but only once per conversation, after which the host asks the person
choices.why: No such rule exists.

prompt: How many tests passed in test_marginalia_mcp.py?

choices.text: The customer's id never leaves the server
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A missing order says why
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The model writes polite replies
